metadata.title: Turkish Test Corpus
metadata.notes: Test fixture. Two Aesop fables and a repetition text, written in English for this fixture and machine-translated into Turkish with Google Translate; the Turkish is the corpus text and the English originals are the sentence translations. Same English source as the chinese-test fixture, so the two are parallel. Tokenisation is the app's own auto-parser. Other annotations are manual.

sentences.text: Sıcak bir öğleden sonra aç bir tilki bahçede yürüyordu.

translations.text: One hot afternoon a hungry fox walked through a garden.
A hot afternoon, a hungry fox was walking through a garden.

sentences.text: Yüksek bir asmada sallanan bir salkım olgun üzüm gördü.

translations.text: He saw a bunch of ripe grapes hanging from a high vine.

sentences.text: Tilki ayağa fırladı ama üzümlere ulaşamadı.

translations.text: The fox jumped up, but he could not reach the grapes.

sentences.text: Tekrar tekrar denedi ama yine de onlara ulaşamadı.

translations.text: He tried again and again, and still he could not reach them.

sentences.text: Sonunda tilki uzaklaşıp üzümlerin ekşi olduğunu söylemiş.

translations.text: At last the fox walked away and said that those grapes were sour.
The fox ran to the river.
The fox ran to the river.

sentences.text: Tilki su içti, sonra tilki tekrar su içti.

translations.text: The fox drank water, and then the fox drank water again.

sentences.text: Nehrin kenarında küçük bir tilki ve büyük bir tilki oturuyordu.

translations.text: A small fox and a big fox sat by the river.
That's a line from the first chapter.

sentences.text: Bu ise bir sonraki bölümden bir cümle.

translations.text: And this is a sentence from the next chapter.
